The segment collection, segment item, segment execute and system settings routes advertise a business domain but are the generic CRUD factory over organization_members: GET returns member roster rows at the member floor, every write is refused, and nothing is segmented, executed or configured. A real member_segments table exists in the governance list and is not bound.

The update-role route is the generic CRUD factory over organization_members, a READ_ONLY table: GET returns member rows at the steward floor and POST is refused, so no role change can occur through it.

The analytics routes (claims, financial, executive, heatmap, comparative, dashboard, deadlines, clause statistics, trends, insights) are the generic CRUD factory over analytics_metrics, trend_analyses or insight_recommendations, which are OPERATIONAL. GET returns stored rows, not computed analytics, and any steward can insert arbitrary rows that are then served as analytics.

The platform user directory and activity feed select organization_members and organizations with no organization predicate at a platform_lead role title and return member name, email and role across organizations. Neither read is audited.

The cross-organization analytics route selects up to 1000 analytics_metrics rows through the global db handle inside a withRLSContext call that names no organization. The source does not show which rows tenant security returns, and the route is gated by a role title.

Member deactivation and removal revoke sessions, the platform-auth membership and the local row in separate stores. The audit record is atomic only with the local status update, and the route returns 502 when a step fails, leaving a partial state for a retry.
Agreement creation reads request.json() with no schema: only the status is checked, and every other field is inserted as supplied at a steward role-title floor.

AI grievance triage, clause reasoning and the copilot read any grievance in the organization for a steward role title. They do not check that the steward holds the case, so grievance content for cases the steward does not represent is sent to a model.

Routes that run enforceAISafety with grievance_legal, confidential or pension_financial data classes call the model with dataClass internal in the service layer. The two vocabularies disagree and the source shows no mapping between them.
Finance analysis and the pension projection, funding and trustee-summary routes read dues, arrears, remittances, trial-balance and pension data for an officer role title, with no financial mandate.

The employer-risk and insight-report GET handlers insert rows (employer_risk_scores, ai_insight_reports) through the global db handle and record the invocation with a separate auditLog event that is not committed with the row.
The classify, match-precedents, summarize and search routes call a model and write no audit event in the route handler or in the service that holds the AI call.
The classify route applies no AI feature gate and no AI safety check, although every sibling AI route applies both.
AI search and summarize return another organization's knowledge row when is_public is true, and no source says who may set the flag. Public cross-tenant data is not authorized by being public.
The semantic-search status GET counts every cba_clause and arbitration_precedents row across organizations through the global db handle with no organization predicate, at the member role floor.
The AI feedback GET returns every user's rating, comment and user id for a query id in the organization at the member role floor.
The AI ingest route indexes documents into a process-local Map, so an indexed document is lost on restart and not shared across instances, while the response reports status indexed.
The embedding cache statistics GET is gated by an organization administrator role title but reports platform-wide cache state.

Signing stores signatureValue ATTESTATION over a document-reference hash. The source says there is no cryptographic signature value, so verification cannot prove who signed or that content is unchanged.

The generic CRUD create copies the whole request body into the insert and the update strips only the primary key and organization column, so a caller can set status, author, approval, cost and provenance columns on every table whose route lists no blockedPatchFields; none of the Gate 0B.3 CRUD routes lists any.

The generic CRUD delete sets status archived on any table with a status column, but the break_status, negotiation_status, proposal_status and arbitration_status enums contain no archived value, so deletion of those records cannot succeed as designed and the failure is not shown by any source.

Break creation at the member floor does not force memberId from the session because the collection route declares an explicit ownerColumn, which sets the factory low-role mode to open, so a member can record a break, with its denial and compliance fields, for another member.
The KPI configuration read returns alert thresholds and the alertRecipients column to every member at the read floor.

Disconnecting a calendar requires the fixed administrator floor of the generic delete, so a member who connected their own calendar cannot disconnect it, and the delete removes the local row holding provider tokens without revoking the provider grant.
The bulk-import route is the generic CRUD factory over organization_members, a READ_ONLY table: GET returns the member roster to staff and POST is refused, so nothing is imported.
The precedent citations, documents and search routes are the generic CRUD factory over arbitration_decisions: they return and change decision rows and serve no citations, documents or search results.

arbitration_decisions has no organization column, so the library routes return every decision row to every organization whatever isPublic or accessRestrictions say, and the row-level-security policy admits any tenant context.
The library delete uses the fixed administrator floor of the generic factory and hard-deletes the row, so an organization administrator can delete a decision that every organization reads.

A steward can insert an insight_recommendations row through the generic factory with an aiReferenceId, confidence score and recommendations of their choosing, and the row is then served as an AI insight.
The weekly summary records an AI invocation naming model analytics-engine and stores confidenceScore 0.83 and fixed recommendation text for a computation that counts events and runs no model.
The synchronized accounting invoice read returns customer names, balances and amounts to every member at the read floor, ahead of any financial mandate.
The invoice create route is the generic factory over external_invoices, a READ_ONLY table: every POST is refused, so the advertised invoice creation does not exist.
The arbitration collection and item routes read and write arbitration rows for any steward of the organization, accept any grievanceId in the body and do not check that the steward holds the case.

bargaining_proposals has no organization column, so the generic factory adds no tenant predicate to reads, updates or deletes and the create accepts any negotiationId; isolation rests only on a row-level-security policy this tranche cannot show is applied.

records.title: The batch invoicing route selects every active subscription across all organizations and generates an invoice for each at an organization administrator role title, returning every organization id.
The invoice replay route selects the invoice and its line items by id with no organization predicate at a steward role floor, so one organization can read another organization invoice.

Invoice generation, invoice replay and trial expiry declare an atomic service audit, but invoice generation records auditLog after its inserts outside a transaction, replay records a separate access event, and trial expiry writes no audit record.

The billing validation route records only application log events and labels ordinary validation failures unauthorized_access or auth_failed, so security monitoring cannot tell an attack from a wrong currency.

The observability sweep writes alert rules, executions and notifications through the module-level db handle and its audit record through the sweep transaction handle; the source shows no proof that they commit together.
The audits list presents audit-log rows as audit engagements and invents status, findings 0 and hasReport false for every row.
The audit item route returns the complete audit_logs row, with details and any recorded address and agent, to an officer role floor with no redaction by reader.

The audits routes read the audit_security audit_logs table, while persistAtomicAudit writes the domains infrastructure audit_logs table, so the routes do not show the audit records the atomic writers produce.

The bargaining-notes GET returns timeline, statistics and session-type results before the visibleToUserId confidentiality filter is applied, and the timeline returns the title of every note of an agreement whatever its confidentiality level.

The bargaining-note item GET and PATCH are the generic factory: a member reads any note by id, including restricted and confidential notes the collection route withholds, and an update skips the agreement check the collection create applies.

Tentative agreement creation verifies the parent negotiation but stores relatedProposalIds and relatedClauseId without verifying that the proposals or clause belong to that negotiation or organization.
Negotiation and tentative-agreement reads sit at the member floor and ignore confidentialityLevel, so strike-vote results, cost ceilings and costed agreements reach every member.

The trial-expiry route passes a payment-method checker that always returns false, so every expired trial of the organization is cancelled whether or not a payment method exists, at a steward role floor.
The send-invoice route generates and stores an invoice and returns it; nothing is delivered, whatever the route name advertises.

Subscription commercial terms are readable at the member floor, pause, resume, invoice generation and trial expiry sit at the steward floor, and update and cancel sit at the secretary_treasurer role title, a union finance role; no source names the office with contract authority.
calculateMetrics stores claim identifiers in the metric metadata and the metrics GET returns that metadata to every member at the member floor.

The metrics routes resolve the organization once in the route wrapper and again in the action through getOrganizationIdForUser, and the action ignores the first, so a user with more than one membership may write to an organization other than the session organization.

The derived case metrics and the weekly summary count pilot telemetry events and present them as case figures; open cases are created minus closed events and overdue cases are breached minus closed events, with no case table read.

The break compliance report returns per-member denied, missed and flagged counts to any steward while the generic break route holds a member to their own rows, so the report is authorized more broadly than the records it is computed from.

The realtime alerts route returns the raw triggerData of alert executions, with SLA-risk, ingestion-failure and payment-failure counts, to every member under a case-suite entitlement, with no redaction and no named reader.

The Google and Microsoft authorization routes pass the session user id as the OAuth state and the callbacks compare the returned state with that same id, and accept a callback with no state at all, so the state is neither unguessable nor single-use and gives no protection against a forged callback.

The provider callbacks are GET handlers that exchange a code and insert or update the connection row holding the provider tokens, and neither the callback nor the member-floor wrapper writes an audit record for the connection, so a state-changing GET leaves no audit evidence.

encryptCalendarToken returns the token unencrypted when no encryption key is configured outside production, and decryptCalendarToken returns any value without the encryption prefix as it is, so a database written without the key holds provider tokens in clear text and never fails.
The connection collection and item reads select the whole external_calendar_connections row, so the stored accessToken and refreshToken values are returned to the browser of the connection owner.

records.title: The connection sync route selects the connection by id and organization only, with no userId predicate and no role above organization membership, so any member can run an import or export through another member provider account.

The sync route proves that the local calendar and event are in the organization but not that the caller owns a personal calendar or may read a personal event, so a member can import into or export from another member personal calendar.

The sync records intent and outcome through performAuditedOperation around an external provider call, and the connection update runs inside that operation without the audit record; the record is not committed with the state change.

The calendar item route supplies lockedAuthCheck to reject another member personal calendar, but the factory invokes it only when beforeUpdate or mergeJsonColumns is configured and never on delete, and the route configures neither, so a steward can still update or delete another member personal calendar.

The calendar events routes filter events by calendar id and organization or by organization alone and never consult calendars.isPersonal or ownerId, which calendar_events does not carry, so a member reads events of another member personal calendar through calendars/[id]/events and staff read every personal event through calendar/events.

Event create and update store a caller-supplied calendarId without verifying that the calendar belongs to the organization or is visible to the caller; the foreign key checks only that a calendar row exists.

No table of the CBA intelligence dataset has an organization column and none of the services filters by organization, so every organization reads, and every administrator or steward writes, one shared dataset; nothing in the source states which organizations may read it or who curates it.

The agreement list, item and export reads apply a review status filter only when the caller supplies one, so extracted agreements, wage adjustments and clauses that are pending, rejected or superseded are returned as the dataset.

Source registration and update, ingestion, seeding and extraction require only an organization administrator role floor, yet they create and change the dataset every organization reads and call external services at the platform expense, so the administrator of any one organization can curate platform-wide data; no source names the platform staff mandate.

A steward of any organization can approve, reject or supersede an extracted record, which sets the review status every organization sees, and the decision records the reviewer role as the literal steward whatever the caller role is.

Extraction, ingestion runs and source seeding declare an atomic service audit, but they record intent and outcome through performAuditedOperation around many separate statements and an external provider call, so the audit record is not committed with the state change.

The benchmark GET inserts a cba_intel_benchmark_snapshots row when save=true, recording the caller user id, and the route and the service write no audit record, so a state-changing GET is both mislabelled as a read and unaudited.

The snapshot history is selected by target agreement only and returns the computedBy user id of whoever saved each snapshot, so a steward of one organization reads the user ids of stewards of other organizations.

The export route asks the service for 10000 rows but listAgreements clamps the limit to 100, so the CSV advertised as an export of the agreements holds at most the first 100 rows and says nothing about it.

Source registration accepts any URL for the base, API, feed and terms addresses, and the ingestion adapters fetch the discovered document URLs from the server with no host allow-list or private-address check, so an administrator can make the platform request internal addresses.

The moderation step returns not flagged when OPENAI_API_KEY is unset and, when the moderation request fails, returns a flagged result with the reason Safety system unavailable that sendMessage then ignores and proceeds, although the code comments call the failure closed; a member message reaches the model unmoderated whenever moderation is absent or down.

The moderation step posts the member message text directly to api.openai.com with a provider key, outside @nzila/ai-sdk which the same file names as the only route for AI calls, so the data-class, budget and audit controls of the AI control plane do not apply to that call.

The message route marks every reply reviewRequired false and passes the literal role member to enforceAISafety whatever the caller role is, although the service describes the output as advisory with human stewardship preserved, so the policy check never sees the caller real role and the response never asks for review.

When the model call fails the service stores a fixed apology as an assistant message with model fallback, and the route returns it as a successful response marked aiGenerated true with the configured deployment name as the model, so an outage is persisted in the transcript and reported as a model reply.

Retrieval selects at most three active knowledge rows of the organization with no ordering and no vector predicate and only then scores them by similarity, so the context sent to the model is an arbitrary subset of the knowledge base rather than the most relevant documents.

The session list and the message read apply no status condition, so archived and deleted sessions stay listed and readable, and the message read applies neither the ai_chatbot entitlement, the AI feature flag, the AI safety check nor a rate limit, so a transcript stays readable after the feature is disabled.

The list, item, tags, compare and search reads run on the system role, which bypasses row-level security, and the only boundary between organizations is a hand-written application predicate; the route comments name this PRIVILEGED_CROSS_TENANT_REVIEW and no kernel decision stands behind it.

The item authority canReadSharedClause admits a federation clause only when the nearest federation ancestor of the caller equals that of the owner, while the list and search predicate admits it whenever the caller federation appears anywhere in the owner hierarchy path, so when federations nest the list and search return clauses the item, tags and compare reads refuse.

The item read returns originalEmployerName and the creator user id to any reader whatever isAnonymized says, and every read returns the owning organization name, so a clause shared as anonymized discloses the employer it was anonymized from.

The item read returns the createdBy user id of the clause, and the tags read returns whole clause_library_tags rows with their createdBy user id, to stewards of other organizations that may read the clause.

A steward of any organization can create or change a clause to sharing level public, which exposes its text to every organization; sharingChangeDenial checks only federation and congress eligibility, and no source names who may publish collective-agreement text.

Clause create, update, sharing update and tag writes store clause text, title, type, dates, anonymization fields and tag names from the body with no schema validation; only sharingLevel and sharedWithOrgIds are checked, so a malformed value reaches the database or throws as an unhandled error.

Clause create stores a caller-supplied originalClauseId that the schema notes as a foreign key to cba_clauses that is not enforced, and the route checks sourceCbaId against the organization but never checks originalClauseId, so a clause can point at another organization clause.

The update overwrites the shared clause text and sharing fields without raising version or setting previousVersionId, and the delete removes the row and its tags permanently, so organizations that compared or cited a clause see it change silently or vanish, and only the audit record remains.

The compare POST increments comparisonCount on rows owned by other organizations under the system role, and the audit record it commits belongs to the comparing organization, so a reader changes data it does not own and the owner has no record of it.

The compare GET returns a usage message with status 200 and performs no comparison, and the compare POST returns commonKeywords as the constant empty list, so part of the advertised analysis is a placeholder presented as a result.

The clc dashboard, remittances and sync routes are the same generic CRUD configuration over clc_sync_log, and no other code in the application reads or writes that table, so the dashboard and remittance routes return and create synchronization log rows and serve no dashboard or remittance, and the sync route records a log entry and starts no synchronization.

The routes read the whole clc_sync_log row, with errorMessage, errorDetails, syncData and dataHash, at the member floor, and the steward create stores any body field, including status, record counts, isVerified, verifiedBy and verifiedAt, so a steward can record a synchronization as verified that never ran and every member can read integration error details.

The CNESST filing collection declares ownerColumn memberId, so the factory compares the uuid memberId column with the session user id for every caller, steward included, while the item routes declare no ownerColumn and let a steward read any filing of the organization; the source does not show that the session user id is the member id, so the collection and the item routes disagree about which filings a steward may see.

The CNESST filing item routes and the create read and write any filing of the organization for a steward role floor, accept any memberId, incidentId and unionRepId in the body, and do not check that the steward represents the member the filing concerns; a filing holds the member injury narrative, outcome and compensation awarded.

anti_scab_violations has no createdBy column, so the factory records no author, reportedById and reportedByName are taken from the body rather than the session, and any steward of the organization can change the outcome fields (resolved, penaltyAmount, injunctionGranted, tatFileNumber) of any violation record.

The anti-scab violation and joint committee tables have no status column, so the fixed administrator delete of the factory removes the regulatory record permanently; only the audit record of the delete remains, and no source names a retention rule for them.

The joint committee read sits at the member floor and returns the worker representative list with member identifiers, names and roles, and the worker co-chair identifier, to every member of the organization.

The agreement detail GET increments collective_agreements.view_count in a tenant transaction whenever includeAnalytics=true, at the member floor, with no audit record, so a read-only operation changes stored state and any member can inflate the counter.

The agreement detail returns clauses and bargaining notes by cbaId alone: getClausesByCBAId and getBargainingNotesByCBA carry no organization predicate, and the clause create stores any cbaId, so a clause written by one organization against another organization agreement id is returned in that agreement detail.

The clause create is the generic factory, which stores the body cbaId, a foreign key to collective_agreements.id that no organization condition guards, so a steward can attach clauses to the agreement of another organization; the organization column is forced from the session but the agreement is not checked.
The clause item GET passes countView true on every request that does not ask for the hierarchy, so each read updates cba_clauses.view_count at the member floor with no audit record.
The clause search route is the generic CRUD configuration over cba_clauses and applies no search term: GET lists clause rows and POST creates a clause, so no search is performed.

The clause comparison groups clauses by type, always returns empty differences and best practices, and returns three fixed recommendation sentences whatever the clauses say; the route returns this as an analysis and, with save true, stores it as the analysis result of a named comparison.
The agreement list passes the caller limit and page, parsed without a ceiling, to the service, which clamps neither, so a member can request an unbounded page of agreements.

With includeNotes=true the agreement detail returns every bargaining note of the agreement whose confidentiality level is public or internal to any member at the member floor, so internal bargaining notes reach members who hold no bargaining role.

collective_agreements.cba_number carries a single unique constraint across every organization, and the create and update routes answer a duplicate with a conflict, so a steward of one organization learns whether any organization holds a given agreement number and cannot use a number another organization holds.

The newsletter delivery status route is gated by the financial_intelligence_suite entitlement, a finance product gate, so the entitlement that decides who may read campaign delivery state is unrelated to the data and to the communications obligation.

Any job id that does not start with campaign-, and any campaign id that is not found, returns status processing with zero counts and a start time of the moment of the request, so a job that does not exist is reported as running.
The status response lists the e-mail address of up to ten failed recipients to any steward holding the entitlement and records no audit of the disclosure.

Case studies are global marketing rows read by every organization and the public, yet create, update and delete sit at the organization admin role floor, so the admin of any one organization can publish, rewrite or remove content shown to all organizations; no source names the platform staff mandate that should hold this write.

The public case-study list and the member item read filter on neither visibility nor publishedAt, and the list status filter reads a status column that case_studies does not have, so unpublished rows and rows marked authenticated are returned to anonymous callers and to members of every organization.

The carbon dashboard and infrastructure routes return emissions totals, regional breakdowns, renewable percentages and optimization advice as literals in the handler, with success true and status 200, for any authenticated caller, so invented measurements are presented as monitoring results.

records.title: The carbon dashboard takes organizationId from the query string, defaults it to union-eyes and echoes it, so the response names an organization chosen by the caller and not the session organization.

The carbon validation route computes a certificationEligible result and a message of Eligible for certification from numbers the caller supplied, with no source for the data points and no record of the check, so an unverified figure yields a certification-shaped answer.

The collection routes of preventive_withdrawals and right_of_refusal_events declare ownerColumn workerId, and neither table has a workerId column, so the factory resolves no owner column and applies no owner condition: the declared owner scope is not applied, and the item routes of the same tables declare no owner scope at all.

Any steward of the organization reads, creates and rewrites any member preventive withdrawal and right-of-refusal record, and accepts memberId, memberName, cneesstFilingId and the outcome fields from the body, without holding the member case; the withdrawal holds the physician name, medical certificate date, reassignment and income replacement amounts, and the refusal holds the reprisal complaint details.

right_of_refusal_events has no status column, so the fixed administrator delete of the factory removes the regulatory record of a refusal and any reprisal complaint permanently; only the audit record of the delete remains, and no source names a retention rule.

The pay equity routes store any body field, including status, results and adjustment amounts, so an officer can record an exercise as adjustments_paid without the intermediate states; the contest deadline and the next maintenance date are plain date columns whose statutory rules (sixty days from posting, every five years) exist only as schema comments, so no source computes or enforces them.

Every cognition engine persists its snapshots as JSON files under ops/ue-cognition at the root of the server checkout, one directory per entity shared by every organization, and keeps tenancy only by filtering subject.orgId after reading every file; there is no table, no row level security and no durability across hosts or restarts, so the derived figures a steward and an administrator read are neither tenant-isolated at rest nor reproducible.

The risk, workload and key-indicator GET routes and the precedent search compute a snapshot and write it to a local file on every call, then record a separate auditLog event; the write is not in the audit transaction, a GET changes stored state, and a failed audit leaves the snapshot behind.

Any steward of the organization requests a risk score, recommended action and rationale for any grievance of the organization, and a precedent search that returns the title of any grievance of the organization, without holding the case or being assigned to it; forCaseId of a precedent search is never checked against the organization.

computeMemberEngagement has no caller in the application or in any other package, so the engagement route and the disengaged-member counts of the executive summary and key indicators read a store that nothing writes, and report an empty list and zero counts with status 200 as if they were measurements.

The workload route returns, for every active steward of the organization, a burnout signal, utilization ratio and recommended reassignments to any steward, so a steward reads a colleague burnout signal and caseload that no source says the colleague or the union agreed to share.

The key-indicator snapshot computes estimated admin hours saved and a dollar return from constants (hours saved per precedent retrieval, per early warning and per reassignment, and a loaded hourly rate), not from measured time; the route comment calls the artefact the one handed to buyers, so an assumption is presented as a result.

The cognition health route reports the platform engine registry, ontology and contract versions and engine counts per domain to any officer of any organization; platform runtime posture is a platform operator concern and no source names which organization role may see it.

Meetings, minutes, decisions, attendance, action items and documents of every committee are readable by any member of the organization, because every read sits at the member role floor and nothing consults committee_memberships; a closed or sensitive committee has no confidentiality.

Attendee member ids, action item assignees, document ids and document file URLs are accepted from the body and stored without being checked against the organization membership, the document register or an allowed storage host, so a record can name a person or file that does not belong to the organization.

The generic meeting update excludes only minutes and their approval fields, so the recorded decisions, the agenda items and the meeting status of a meeting whose minutes were approved can still be rewritten by a steward; the approved record is not frozen.
The user who recorded the minutes may also approve them, because approval needs only the officer floor, which includes every higher role, and no check compares the approver with the recorder.

A synthesis requested for one committee with no committeeIds in the body gathers the completed minutes of every committee of the organization and files the result under the committee in the path, so the minutes of committees the requester may not follow are summarized into another committee record.
The meeting and intelligence list routes pass parseInt of the limit and offset query strings straight to the query: there is no maximum, and a value that is not a number reaches the database as NaN.
The committee row returned to every member includes the notes and customFields columns and the contact e-mail, which no source marks as steward-only.

The intelligence POST stores and returns a snapshot whose summary reads Full AI synthesis pending integration, with empty themes, positions and recommendations and a null model, as a successful 200 result, so a stored placeholder is presented as a synthesis.

The generic campaign create and update accept any body field, including status, sentAt, completedAt and the stats counters, so a steward can record a campaign as sent or completed and set its delivery and open figures by hand; no state machine or delivery process owns those fields.

A campaign row stores a segment id, a free-form segment query and an audience count, and no route in the campaign group evaluates the audience, checks the communication preferences or consent of a recipient, or sends; authoring is detached from the consent and delivery rules the platform keeps elsewhere.

The campaign analytics, schedule and send-test paths are the generic campaign item route: analytics returns the campaign row and no analytics, schedule is an unvalidated update of the same row, send-test sends nothing, and a DELETE of any of the three archives the campaign.
message_templates has no status column, so the fixed administrator delete removes a template permanently; campaigns that referenced it lose the link (set null) and no source names a retention rule.
The template duplicate path is the generic template item route: GET returns the template, PATCH rewrites it and DELETE removes it, and nothing duplicates a template.

newsletter_distribution_lists has no status column, so the fixed administrator delete removes the list permanently, and newsletter_list_subscribers deletes with it (on delete cascade), erasing the subscribed, unsubscribed and unsubscribedAt rows that are the suppression and consent trail of the list.
The subscriber list route returns the whole subscriber row, with e-mail address and profile id, of an organization list to any member of the organization, and records no audit of the disclosure.

The SMS message, campaign and conversation creates insert the body as a row, including status, twilioSid, price, sent and delivered times and counts, and send nothing: the Twilio send lives in a service that no route of the group imports, so a steward records messages as sent and delivered that were never sent.

Callers below steward are held to their own rows by the low-role guard, but any steward reads the phone number and message text of every member conversation of the organization, without holding the member case.
sms_campaigns has no owner or personal column, so the low-role guard leaves it open: any member of the organization reads every SMS campaign with its message text, recipient filter and total cost.

The conversation read path is the generic SMS message collection route: it ignores the conversation id, GET lists every message of the organization, and POST inserts a message row; nothing marks a conversation read.

Open and click tracking read the campaign stats object, add one in the handler and write the whole object back as separate statements under the system role, so concurrent events lose counts and the system-role writes leave no audit record.

The unsubscribe route updates the message log, the campaign stats, the communication preference and the consent record as separate statements with no transaction, so a failure part-way leaves a recipient marked unsubscribed in one table and subscribed in another.

A link without a campaign id updates the recipient communication preferences of every organization but writes no consent_records row, so the revocation has no evidentiary record and no organization attribution.

The unsubscribe route changes the campaign message log, the preference and the consent record and never touches newsletter_list_subscribers, so a member who unsubscribes from a campaign link stays subscribed on the distribution lists.

polls is READ_ONLY and poll_votes is DENIED in the CRUD governance table, so no route of the group can create a poll or record or read a vote; the member poll capability exists in schema and URL shape and cannot run through any of these routes.
The poll item path is configured as a collection route, so GET ignores the poll id and lists every poll of the organization.

The generic survey create and update accept any body field, including status, publishedAt, closesAt, responseCount, viewCount and completionRate, so the published state and the response counters are set by hand and not derived from the responses.
The survey list and item reads sit at the member floor and apply no status or publication filter, so a draft survey is readable by every member of the organization.

The survey response read returns respondent name, e-mail, user id, IP address and user agent of every response to any steward, whatever the survey allowAnonymous setting says; an anonymous survey is not anonymous.

The responses route ignores the survey id of its path: GET lists the responses of every survey of the organization, and POST takes surveyId from the body and checks nothing about the survey, so a response is accepted for a draft or closed survey, a second response is accepted when allowMultipleResponses is false, and authentication is not required when the survey says it is.

No route under app/api writes survey_answers, and the results route is the only one that reads the table, so a response can be created and no answer can be recorded; the survey capability cannot be completed through these routes.

The survey results route filters responses and questions by the survey id of the path and applies no organization predicate, does not request a tenant context, and also selects every row of survey_answers of every organization into memory and discards it; the isolation of the count and the question list rests on an ambient database policy the route does not set, and the full-table read is a cross-tenant read of answer text.

The certifications/generate, certifications/renewal-reminders, completions/certificates and notification-preferences paths are the training_courses generic CRUD under action-sounding names: they generate no certificate, send no reminder, list no certificate and store no preference, and a POST creates a course.

The programs/[id]/enrollments and sessions/[id]/attendance item routes read the path id as a training_courses id, so no program enrollment or session attendance is read or written: PATCH rewrites any course field and the administrator DELETE removes the course row permanently because the table has no status column.

The completions route is described as completed registrations only but is configured with no completed condition: GET returns every course_registrations row of the caller and POST inserts any registration, completed or not.

The completions POST writes course_registrations through the factory with no beforeCreate hook, so it skips the organization checks on courseId and sessionId that the registrations route added, and a steward can insert a registration for any member id that references a course or session of another organization.

The registrations, completions and certifications collection reads add memberId equal to the session user id at every role, including steward and administrator, while a steward POST can create rows for any member id: no office can list or verify the training records of another member, and the creating steward cannot read the row back.

The registrations POST is open to a member and its beforeCreate hook forces only memberId, so the member body also stores completed, passed, finalGrade, certificateIssued, certificateNumber, approvedBy, feePaid and feeWaived on their own registration.

The registrations POST checks only that courseId and sessionId exist in the organization: it does not check that the session belongs to the course, that registration is open, that the session has capacity, or that the member is not already registered, and it does not update the session registration count.

The sessions GET returns every column of every session of the organization to any member, including the virtual meeting URL and access code, session budget, actual cost, accommodation hotel and internal notes of sessions the member is not registered for.

The sessions POST stores courseId from the body without checking that the course belongs to the session organization, and the registration, attendance and completion counters and the average rating are plain body-writable columns, so a steward can attach a session to another organization course and write its statistics.

The certifications POST is a free-form insert: courseId, sessionId and registrationId are optional, nothing checks that the member completed anything, and verified defaults to true, so a steward can create a verified certification, including its verifier, revocation and badge fields, with no link to a completed course.

course_code, session_code and certification_number are unique across all organizations rather than within one, so a code used by one organization makes another organization insert fail and the conflict reveals that the code exists.

The education admin screens call operations the route files do not export or do not perform: POST on the attendance and enrollments item routes that export only GET, PATCH and DELETE, PATCH and DELETE with an id query on the session, program and certification collection routes that export only GET and POST, and renewal reminders on a route that runs the course create, so the screens cannot mark attendance, enroll, edit or delete sessions, programs and certifications, or send reminders, and ignored filters (memberId, sessionStatus, includeProgress) return unfiltered rows.

Both reminder queries name columns the training schema does not define (course_sessions session_date, session_time, location and duration_hours; member_certifications certificate_number; training_courses continuing_education_hours) and compare the boolean provides_certification to a certification name, so against the declared schema the job fails at its first query and sends nothing; the route test mocks the database and cannot show it.

The reminder job selects every registered member and every expiring certification holder across all organizations without consulting communication preferences or consent, and records no sent marker, so a member who opted out is still e-mailed and a second run on the same day sends the same reminder again.

The reminder job returns success true and the message "Education reminders processed successfully" whatever the counts, so a run in which every send failed (including an unconfigured e-mail service) reads as success, and the failure list in the response carries member e-mail addresses.

The reminder job sends one message at a time with a 100 ms pause and no cap on recipients, across every organization in one request, so the run time grows with the member count and has no resume point if the request is cut off.

The content training list and the content statistics report completions as the number of registrations with attended true, not completed true, so a member who attended without finishing counts as a completion and the figure shown to every member does not match the completed flag of the registration.

The content training list has no row limit, and the content templates list takes its limit from the query string with no upper bound and no validation, so a caller can request an arbitrarily large page and a negative value reaches the database as a SQL error.

The content templates GET returns cms_pages rows of every status (draft, review, archived and published) to any member of the organization, with the author user id, and ignores the allowed_roles restriction of the row, although the status workflow reserves drafting to content managers and publishing to administrators.

The content status transition checks the role for each step but not who prepared the item, so one administrator can move an item from draft through review to published alone, and republishing rewrites published_at.

The remittance run detail route is open to any member of the organization, takes no financial mandate and reads through the shared db import instead of an explicit withRLSContext call, and returns the run, its items and every artifact of the run, including the stored remittance CSV and JSON whose content holds the external employee id with gross pay, dues, benefit, pension and net pay of every employee; the payroll run detail beside it requires the secretary_treasurer role and a live view mandate, and the dashboard layout restricts the whole area to administrators.

The replay route checks the secretary_treasurer role and the replay entitlement only and never calls requireLiveFinancialMandate, so it neither requires a live financial mandate nor limits the run to the records a view grant names, yet it reads every payroll item of any run of the organization, returns per-employee gross, net, dues, benefit and pension differences, and appends evidence artifacts; prepare, approve, execute, view and remittance all require a mandate.

Every replay request inserts a new replay row, three evidence artifacts attached to the source run, an evidence link and, when the replay differs, an open error-severity inconsistent_replay_results event against the source run, with no idempotency key and no unique replay key; approveRun counts open error events for the run and refuses approval until each is acknowledged, so repeated or deliberately different replays, which any caller of the replay route can request at any run status, add approval blockers and evidence rows to the run they only read.

The replay mode enum holds only exact and simulated, and the route stores simulated for new_rule and exact for both exact and new_engine, so a replay under a different engine version is recorded as an exact replay and the stored mode cannot tell an engine change from a faithful re-run.

The seal action of the payroll run PATCH route, named execute in its mandate action and in its audit and compliance record ("Official payroll run executed (posted)"), only sets status posted, executor and timestamp on the run: no ledger entry, payment, deduction or remittance is written, and the remittance route refuses a run that is no longer approved, so a posted run reads as executed while nothing was done with its amounts.

Timesheet ingest never writes member_employment_id or job_classification_id on an entry, payroll preparation therefore opens a blocking critical missing_employment_mapping event for every official run, approveRun refuses approval while a critical blocking event is open, and no route of the employer execution API sets the mapping or resolves a critical event, so an official payroll run cannot reach approval through this API.

The evidence seal of payroll, remittance and replay evidence is sha256 of the entity type, run id and manifest hash with no key, signature or external anchor, stored as an artifact named evidence-seal.sig beside the manifest it covers, and the chain verification compares stored parent seal hashes and depths only and never recomputes a manifest or seal hash, so anyone able to write the artifact rows can rewrite a chain that still verifies.

Payroll preparation stores the period from the request body instead of the period of the validated timesheet batch, derives the rule version from the first entry shift date, reads the batch and the already-approved check through the shared connection outside the transaction that inserts the run, takes no lock, and names the run with a millisecond timestamp under a non-unique run code index, so two concurrent requests both pass the check and both create official runs for one batch.

The remittance CSV writes the external employee id taken from the uploaded timesheet file into the first column with no quoting and no neutralisation of a leading formula character, and the three remittance items (dues, benefits, pension) each report the number of payroll items as their member count, even when the amount of the group is zero, so the package can carry spreadsheet formulas and member counts the data does not support.

Any steward can ingest the timesheet file whose rows become the dues, benefit and pension amounts of a payroll run, with no financial mandate and a role floor below the secretary_treasurer role the later duties need; the csv content and the employee external ids are unbounded free text that is never matched to a member or employment record, and the parser splits on commas without quoting.

A steward can persist a compliance event with any event code, severity, summary, details and blocking flag against any payroll or remittance run of the organization, with no financial mandate; the codes are free text, so an event can imitate one the system raises, and an open critical blocking event or an open error event stops approveRun, while no route in this API resolves a critical event.

The compliance event list and the timesheet batch list are open to any member of the organization, unbounded and unpaged, without a financial mandate: they return every compliance event with its details JSON and every batch with the uploader id, file name and validation summary, although the dashboard layout restricts the area to administrators and the payroll run reads require a mandate.

Any steward reads, unbounded and without a read audit record, the names, e-mail addresses, telephone numbers, notes and custom fields of every employer representative in the organization, through the employer rows (primary and labour-relations contacts, business numbers, notes, customFields) and the employer contacts list.

The employer create and update accept parentCompanyId from the body through the generic factory, and the column is a foreign key to employers.id with no organization condition, so an employer of one organization can name an employer of another organization as its parent company, and the foreign key outcome tells the caller whether that id exists.

The employer delete sets status archived only: archivedAt stays empty and nothing checks the employer for open timesheet batches, contacts or communications, and the timesheet ingest looks the employer up by id and organization without testing its status, so an archived employer keeps receiving payroll input.

The communications POST route only inserts a row: it imports and calls no mail, SMS, letter or notification provider, takes the status from the caller, stamps sentAt when the caller says sent, hard-codes the sender name System, and then emits the employer.communication_sent audit event, so a record of type email with status sent reads as a delivered message although nothing was sent.

The communications POST route stores employerId, grievanceId, recipientContactId and templateId from the body without checking that any of them belongs to the organization, although the contacts route verifies its employer; employer_id has no foreign key, grievance_id and recipient_contact_id are foreign keys with no organization condition, so a communication can be attached to another organization grievance or contact, or to an employer that does not exist.

Any steward of the organization lists every employer communication, subject and body included, with the grievance each is linked to, unbounded and without holding the grievance or a case office, so grievance correspondence is readable beyond the stewards who represent the member.

After the transaction that commits the row and its atomic audit record, the contacts and communications POST routes emit a second audit event through auditLog; in the canonical state that write appends the audit chain row through its own withRLSContext call and does not swallow a failure, so the route catches it and returns a 500 although the row is already committed, and the contacts event carries the contact name in its details.

The contacts POST route stores isPrimary from the body and clears no other contact of the employer, and the table has no unique primary-contact rule, so an employer can hold many primary contacts and a consumer cannot tell which one is current.

The audit log read returns every column of the latest hundred audit rows of the organization (IP address, user agent, session and correlation ids, old and new values, error text and metadata) to any officer, ignores the limit the page sends, offers no filter or page and is itself not audited.

An administrator writes entries into the audit trail with a free resource type, a resource id and metadata keys that are not checked against any record of the organization; the entry is marked compliance.manual_entry but shares the trail and the table with system-recorded actions.

Any member of the organization reads every commercial contract of the organization (value, signer, billing account and subscription ids, renewal and termination terms) and the priced line items of any contract through an unbounded full-row select, behind a module entitlement and a member role floor; no office is named for contract terms.

The contract create takes billingAccountId and subscriptionId from the body and inserts them without checking that they belong to the organization, so a contract can be bound to another tenant billing account or subscription; the contract and line items also accept caller-set prices and a total contract value as free text.

createContract calls auditLog inside its transaction, but auditLog writes through its own connection and logs a failed write without throwing, so the contract and its line items can commit with no audit record, or the audit record can remain after a rollback.
The compliance alert and report reads catch every error and answer success with an empty list, so a failed query is reported to the steward as no alerts and no reports.

No route, service or job inserts into compliance_alerts or employer_reports, so the alert and report reads, and the compliance metrics the leadership dashboard computes from the alerts, are over tables that nothing populates.
The alert and report lists have no limit or page, and the report list returns the whole free-form JSON document of every report of every employer of the organization.

The validate route returns compliant, warning and violation verdicts with a severity and a recommendation computed only from dates and counts the caller sends in the body; nothing is checked against a grievance, vote or certification record, nothing is persisted or audited, and any authenticated user with an organization may obtain a verdict.

The arbitration deadline falls back to a literal thirty days when its rules lookup returns nothing, the lookup is an unauthenticated self-call whose failure is swallowed by an empty catch, the strike vote quorum is a literal fifty percent without a legal reference and the certification card thresholds are literals for three jurisdictions, with no check at all for any other.

The validate body is cast to an interface and never parsed: a schema is declared in the file and is not used, dates are passed to Date without a validity check, and an unknown jurisdiction or check name yields no check and no error.

The employer data firewall policy table is readable by every member and has no write path (the CRUD governance table refuses writes), and no service reads its block flags to withhold strike plans, membership lists or internal discussions from employer-facing paths.

The COPE campaign, canvassing and officials routes are one generic CRUD factory over donation_campaigns under three political names; no political campaign, canvassing or official table is reachable from the application schema, so the interfaces that call the routes receive donation rows without the fields they render.

A steward creates a campaign row through the generic factory with any body field, including currentAmount (funds raised), status and the payment product and price identifiers, and any member reads those rows.

The assignment inserts any member uuid from the body without checking that it belongs to the organization or is eligible, into a table with no organization column that cannot be scoped to a tenant afterwards, and the request create stores any employer uuid without checking it is an employer of the organization.

The assignment ignores the status of the request and the assignments it already has: a cancelled, expired or filled request accepts more assignments and has its status rewritten, the same member can be offered twice, and filled is derived from the length of the one posted list.

The seniority, rotation, availability and skills ranking and the organization rules table exist, but no route calls the ranking and no route writes a rule, so the assignment is whatever member list the officer posts and the fairness the hall model describes is not applied.
When the stats query fails the route logs the error and answers 200 with every count at zero, so a database failure reads on the dashboard as an organization with no claims and no members.

The leadership compliance metrics report deadline adherence and documentation rate as 100 when there are no alerts, and nothing writes alerts; the grievance aggregates silently stop at the first five thousand rows and the alerts at one thousand; the figures are cached per organization.

The CSV export is guarded by authentication alone, with no organization, role or entitlement, and its data source is not wired: production answers 501, every other environment answers 200 with an empty file; once wired the case export would carry case ids, assignees and worksites with no organization predicate in the route.

The enterprise data subject request route is the generic factory over a subject-owned table with no owner column, so every read and write is refused with a 403 that names a dedicated route, and the dedicated privacy route answers 501; no request can be received, and the table has no organization column to scope a request to the institution that must answer it.

The enterprise integrations route is the generic factory over oauth_providers, a per-user table of provider account ids and access and refresh tokens with no organization column, under a name that advertises an organization integration list; the governance table denies it, so it serves nothing, and lifting that denial would expose tokens at the member floor.

The generic CRUD route declares orgScoped true over a table that has no organization column, so the factory adds no tenant predicate and every row of the table is visible to every organization once the read is allowed; the declared scope is a no-op.

The debug user-role route has no environment guard: it is the generic factory over organization_members, so it returns the roster rows of the organization (name, e-mail, phone, role, hire date, membership number, exemption reason) to a steward or above, and the caller own full row to a member, instead of a role check.

The Resend webhook looks the event up by provider message id and, when no message_log row carries it, logs a warning and still answers 200, so the provider does not retry and the delivery, bounce or complaint event is lost; an event that arrives before the sender has stored the provider message id is lost the same way.

The webhook sets message_log.status to the status of whichever event arrives last with no ordering rule, so a late sent, delivered or opened event overwrites a bounced, failed or complained status, and it updates in place a table whose schema comment declares it an immutable delivery log with no updatedAt.

The Svix message id is used only as a detail of the delivery-ledger row: the failed, unsubscribed and complained branches increment the campaign statistics on every redelivery of the same event, and the statistics are rewritten as a whole object from a value read earlier in the transaction, so a retry or a concurrent event changes the counters wrongly.

A complaint or suppression event updates the existing communication_preferences row of the one organization and recipient on the message log row, never inserts one and never writes a consent record or touches the distribution-list subscriptions, so a recipient with no preference row stays emailable while the audit record says the suppression was applied, and the same address is not suppressed in any other organization.

The delivery-ledger callback runs after the message_log transaction has committed and its result (recorded, duplicate, unmatched, ambiguous) is ignored, so a ledger failure answers 500 after the message_log, statistics and suppression have already changed and the provider retry repeats them, and an unmatched or ambiguous ledger event is acknowledged without a trace.

message_log.provider_message_id has neither an index nor a unique constraint, yet every webhook event selects by it with limit 1 under the system role, so each event scans the table and, if two rows ever carried the same id, the organization that receives the event is arbitrary.

The public contact route has no local store: it forwards the submission to HubSpot and answers ok true even when HUBSPOT_API_KEY is unset or the upsert fails (both return null and the handler skips the deal), so a visitor is told the message was received when no record of it exists anywhere but a log line that omits the message text.

The only control on the public contact route is a 20-per-hour limit keyed on cf-connecting-ip, x-real-ip or the first x-forwarded-for value, all request headers a caller can set unless an edge strips them, and the route has no captcha, honeypot or origin check, so a script can rotate the header and flood the CRM with contacts and deals.

Only the message field has a length bound on the public contact form: first name, last name, organization, role and inquiry type are unbounded strings forwarded to HubSpot (limited only by the 16 KiB body cap), and the visitor e-mail address and organization are written to the application log at info level.

The continuity archives and docs paths are byte-identical wrappers that re-export the document repository handlers behind a placeholder requireOrgAccess that always returns true and a mutation boundary that only checks that a method string exists: no archive, retention, continuity-plan or succession behaviour exists behind the names, a POST uploads an ordinary document, and the dead unauthorized branch reads as an access check that is not there.

The document repository list that the continuity paths serve has no row limit and no page, returns every non-deleted document row of the organization joined to its links, then runs a case-access lookup for each grievance-linked row and applies the linkedCase filter and the visibility policy in memory, so the cost grows with the size of the organization document store.

The continuity inheritance path advertises succession records but is the generic CRUD factory over pending_profiles, the pre-signup profile table holding the e-mail, Whop membership id and usage credits, which the CRUD governance table lists as DENIED, so every read and write answers 403 and no inheritance record can be read or written.

The inheritance route sets orgScoped true over pending_profiles, which has no organization column, so the factory adds no tenant predicate; the support_agent read floor and the DENIED governance entry are the only barriers, and lifting the governance entry would list the pre-signup e-mail and payment identifiers of every organization.

The deprecation registry served to every member names canonical replacements that have no route (/api/billing/reports, /api/strike/fund and /api/messages/[id]), repeats the sunset instant 2026-07-07 as a literal instead of the SUNSET_DATE constant, promises removal after that instant although routes it lists (payments webhook stripe, messaging preferences, financial vendors) still exist, and gives no sign that the list is hand-maintained.

The document-intake reaper, external-data-sync, location-retention and monthly-per-capita handlers export the same function as GET and POST, so a GET (the method a scheduler, browser prefetch or monitoring probe issues) expires intakes, deletes stored objects and location data, calls external providers or writes per-capita remittances while the route manifest records the GET as a read.

No scheduler entry in the repository invokes the document-intake reaper, external-data-sync, monthly-per-capita, observability-alerts or sla-watchdog handlers: apps/union-eyes/vercel.json schedules only calendar-sync and the ue-v2 apps.bicep cron job calls only deadline-reminders, so the jobs run only if an operator wires a trigger outside the source.

The two handlers listed in CRON_API_ROUTES (external-data-sync and monthly-per-capita) are first checked in proxy.ts against CRON_SECRET only with a plain !== comparison and the x-cron-secret header only, while the handler accepts CRON_SECRET_KEY first, a Bearer value too, and compares with timingSafeEqual; where only CRON_SECRET_KEY is set the edge refuses a correct caller, and the edge check is not constant time.

The only scheduler entry for calendar-sync (vercel.json, every 15 minutes) names the path with no method or secret, while the route exports POST only and verifyCronAuth reads only the x-cron-secret header, so a trigger that issues GET or presents the secret as a Bearer value is refused and no connection is synced.

The Google and Microsoft event import loops catch and discard the error of each event, and the cancelled-event handler discards its own error but the caller still adds one to the deleted count, so a failed event is missing from the local calendar while the connection is marked synced, the audit record reports the counts and the response shows no failure.

The Google import asks for at most 2500 events in one list call and never follows nextPageToken, and the cron never passes the stored sync token, so events beyond the first page are not imported while the connection is marked synced; the due list is selected without a lock or claim and nextSyncAt moves only at the end of each connection, so an overlapping run repeats the same provider calls.

The intake object finalizer selects only rows whose deletion_attempts are below INTAKE_MAX_DELETION_ATTEMPTS, so an abandoned object whose deletion keeps failing is never selected again after the limit, stays in storage, and the response reports only the failures of the current run.

The external-data-sync handler returns a plain object in every case, including the outer failure branch that sets success false, so the response is HTTP 200 whatever fails, and each sync method writes the external_data_sync_log row as completed even when records failed and never stores the collected error list, so the log does not show a partial or failed run.

syncContributionRates (and its sync-log rows) selects, updates and inserts through the plain tenant db handle while the wage, union-density and COLA methods run inside withSystemContext, so the contribution-rate part of the scheduled job runs without the system authority the other three parts were given and does not commit with a system transaction.

The 24-hour member location retention is enforced only by the location-retention handler, whose comments say it runs hourly, but no scheduler entry in the repository invokes it (vercel.json lists only calendar-sync and apps.bicep only deadline-reminders), so expired location points and geofence events are deleted only if an operator wires a trigger outside the source.

The deletion log written by the retention job records the run time as both the oldest and the newest deleted record date instead of the real dates, carries no organization, no list of affected members and no audit_log record, and the location tables have no organization column, so the evidence of what was deleted cannot show whose data or from when.

The retention job loads every expired user id from both tables without a limit and deletes user by user inside one system transaction, so a backlog (for example after the job did not run) is one long transaction holding locks on the live location tables.
